summary: The new face in the room: {the newcomer} comes over to introduce themselves and the player decides how much room to make.
realLife: One life: A University of Illinois study of engineers at a large manufacturer: about 65 percent of what new hires learned came from coworkers and 15 percent from managers. A local mentor, a meaningful early assignment and social invitations outside work helped; many newcomers left in two years. Another: A woman of 55 renovating a new house in Detroit heard a knock; her neighbor in her 90s brought a gift and the two found a shared love of architecture and became best friends. Another: Next-door neighbors for years without meeting. Their dogs met at the gate; a 79-year-old asked a 31-year-old for advice on talking with her grandson, and both told hard stories. The older woman said the friendship changed her plans for her future. Another: A University of Kansas study of 467 people (355 adults who had recently moved): moving from acquaintance to casual friend took roughly 40 to 60 hours together, and work hours counted for much less than relaxed time.
